_comment: The real captains of the age (scripts/bonds.gd history_day). Each joins the roster of named captains on `from`, in their real ship out of their real haunt, and then lives their life step by step: `life` is dated steps, each with news `text` and any of ship/type (a new ship; also brings them back to sea after `gone`), faction (a pardon or a new commission), haunt, gone (leaves the Caribbean, alive), dies (their historical end), effects (scripts/economy/effects.gd, as in history.json), port (the news travels from there at sailing speed), unless_flag (an event flag that stops the step, e.g. rogers_stopped). They keep to the histories only while you leave them be: a bond of any kind (a fight starts a rivalry) takes them off the script, and their story is their own. Flags set: fate_<id> when the histories' end comes, gone_<id> when they die by any hand. Dates checked against Woodard, The Republic of Pirates, and Rediker, Villains of All Nations; where a date is only known to the season, the first of the month is used. Stats and skills (0-20) and fame are design choices.

de_graaf.name: Laurens de Graaf
de_graaf.bio: A Dutch gunner who turned buccaneer, sailing under French commissions out of Saint-Domingue. The Spanish call him Lorencillo.
de_graaf.arrive: In the taverns of Tortuga they drink to Lorencillo: Laurens de Graaf, the Dutchman with a French commission and a gunner's eye.

life.text: De Graaf has taken the Spanish payship Princesa off Puerto Rico, with the garrisons' silver aboard, and made her his own.
De Graaf, Grammont and Van Hoorn have taken Veracruz by night and held the town to ransom for a fortnight.
De Graaf, now a French officer, has landed on Jamaica and burned the plantations east of Port Royal.
De Graaf has sailed north with Iberville to plant a French colony on the Mississippi. The Caribbean will not see Lorencillo again.

grammont.name: Michel de Grammont
grammont.bio: A gentleman of Paris who killed a man over his sister, went to sea, and became the chief of the buccaneers of Saint-Domingue.
grammont.arrive: Michel de Grammont, 'the General' of the buccaneers, keeps a table at Petit-Goave and a fleet in the offing.

life.text: Grammont has taken Campeche, and when the Spanish would not ransom it, burned it after the bonfires for the feast of Saint Louis.
Grammont sailed north to raid the Florida coast, and has not been seen since. The Hardi is lost with all her people.

hornigold.name: Benjamin Hornigold
hornigold.bio: A privateer of the last war who never stopped. He takes Spanish and French prizes, but will not fire on an English ship.
hornigold.arrive: Benjamin Hornigold has made a pirates' nest of Nassau, and he's teaching a new generation the trade.

life.text: Hornigold's crew have voted him out for refusing to take English ships. Most went with Sam Bellamy; Hornigold keeps the Ranger and a few loyal hands.
Benjamin Hornigold has taken the King's Pardon from Captain Pearse of HMS Phoenix at Nassau. He'll hunt his old friends now.
Hornigold, hunting for Governor Rogers, has brought John Auger and his crew back to Nassau to hang.
Benjamin Hornigold's ship has struck a reef somewhere between New Spain and New Providence. He is lost with most of her people.

bellamy.name: Samuel Bellamy
bellamy.bio: A West Country sailor who came out to dive on the Spanish wrecks and stayed to rob the rich. His crews call themselves Robin Hood's men.
bellamy.arrive: A young West Country captain, Sam Bellamy, has joined Hornigold's company at Nassau in the sloop Marianne. The men love him.

life.text: Bellamy has taken the galley Sultana and mounted guns on her. Half of Hornigold's men have gone over to him.
Bellamy has taken the Whydah in the Windward Passage, homeward bound with gold and ivory, and made her his flagship.
The Whydah has gone down in a nor'easter off Cape Cod with Sam Bellamy and more than a hundred of his men. Two came ashore alive.

la_buse.name: Olivier "La Buse" Levasseur
la_buse.bio: A Calais man, schooled and well-born, who came out a privateer and went pirate with Hornigold. They call him the Buzzard.
la_buse.arrive: Olivier Levasseur, the Frenchman they call La Buse, the Buzzard, sails with Hornigold and Bellamy in the Postillion.

life.text: La Buse has sailed for the coast of Africa, and from there, they say, for the Indian Ocean.
News from the far side of the world: La Buse has been hanged at Saint-Denis on the Isle of Bourbon. They say he threw a cipher to the crowd: 'Find my treasure, he who can.'

blackbeard.name: Edward "Blackbeard" Teach
blackbeard.bio: Hornigold's pupil, a huge man who plaits his beard with ribbons and goes into a fight with slow-match smoking under his hat. He has killed nobody that anyone knows of. He has never needed to.
blackbeard.arrive: Edward Teach, the one they call Blackbeard, has taken over the gentleman-pirate Stede Bonnet's sloop Revenge, and Bonnet with it.

life.text: Blackbeard has taken the French ship La Concorde off Martinique, mounted forty guns on her, and renamed her the Queen Anne's Revenge.
Blackbeard has blockaded Charles Town in Carolina for a week, and ransomed its leading men for a chest of medicines.
The Queen Anne's Revenge has run aground at Beaufort Inlet. Teach has marooned half his crew, and sails on in the sloop Adventure with the loot.
Blackbeard is dead, killed at Ocracoke by Lieutenant Maynard of the Royal Navy.

vane.name: Charles Vane
vane.bio: The hardest of the Nassau men. He spat on the King's Pardon, and he's cruel to the crews he takes. Whether he's brave is another matter.
vane.arrive: Charles Vane has refused the King's Pardon and taken the brigantine Ranger. Nassau's diehards follow him now.

life.text: Charles Vane has sent a burning prize down on Governor Rogers' warships and escaped Nassau under the black flag.
Vane's crew have voted him out for refusing to fight a French man-of-war. Jack Rackham, his quartermaster, has the Ranger now.
Charles Vane, wrecked in the Bay of Honduras and recognised by an old acquaintance, has been hanged at Gallows Point, Port Royal.

rackham.name: John "Calico Jack" Rackham
rackham.bio: Vane's quartermaster, in calico breeches and a gaudy coat. All show, they say; the two women who sail with him are the real thing.
rackham.arrive: Calico Jack Rackham has turned Vane off his own ship and taken command of the Ranger.

life.text: Calico Jack Rackham has come into Nassau and taken the King's Pardon from Governor Rogers. He's ashore, and keeping company with Anne Bonny.
Rackham has broken his pardon and stolen the sloop William out of Nassau harbour. Anne Bonny sails with him, and Mary Read.
Rackham, taken off Negril Point by Jonathan Barnet's privateer, has been hanged at Gallows Point.

roberts.name: Bartholomew "Black Bart" Roberts
roberts.bio: A Welsh mate taken by pirates off Africa, elected captain within six weeks. He drinks tea, keeps strict articles, and takes more ships than any man alive.
roberts.arrive: Bartholomew Roberts is in the Leeward Islands with the Royal Fortune, fresh from burning the fishing fleet at Newfoundland.

life.text: Roberts has taken a French man-of-war off Martinique, hanged a governor from her yardarm, they say, and made her his new Royal Fortune.
Roberts has sailed for the coast of Africa with his squadron.
Off Cape Lopez, HMS Swallow has caught Bartholomew Roberts. Grapeshot tore out his throat; his crew put him over the side in his finery, as he asked.
